review:
SUMMARY: 8 confirmed bugs identified across task management, serialization, event notification, RPC push, protobuf parsing, publisher lifecycle, snapshot writing, and pattern matching. All reproduce reliably and include verified fixes.

POINTS:
- [common/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/common/task/BatchTaskCounter.java:52] Calling batchSuccess(0) or negative causes IndexOutOfBoundsException due to missing lower-bound check — fix: change guard to `if (batch >= 1 && batch <= batchCounter.size())`
- [consistency/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/consistency/serialize/HessianSerializer.java:61] String.format called as instance method instead of static, causing NoSuchMethodError at runtime — fix: use `String.format("%s cannot be cast to %s", ...)`
- [common/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/common/notify/NotifyCenter.java:383] deregisterPublisher throws NullPointerException when publisher is null for unregistered event type — fix: add null check before calling `publisher.shutdown()`
- [core/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/core/remote/RpcPushService.java:79-91] Push failures silently reported as success when connection is closed or null — fix: call `requestCallBack.onFail()` instead of `onSuccess()` in failure paths
- [consistency/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/consistency/ProtoMessageUtil.java:49-60] parse(null) or empty array silently swallows NPE/AIOOBE and returns incorrect results — fix: add guard `if (bytes == null || bytes.length == 0) throw new ConsistencyException(...)`
- [common/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/common/notify/DefaultSharePublisher.java:63-78] removeSubscriber unconditionally removes subscriber from global set, breaking delivery for other registered event types — fix: only remove from global set if subscriber has no remaining registered event types
- [consistency/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/consistency/snapshot/Writer.java:59-62] addFile stores caller's LocalFileMeta reference directly, allowing caller-side mutations to corrupt stored state — fix: store a defensive copy `files.put(fileName, new LocalFileMeta(meta))`
- [common/src/main/java/com/alibaba/nacos/common/utils/FuzzyGroupKeyPattern.java:109-112] matchPattern and getNamespaceFromPattern throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on malformed patterns missing splitter — fix: add bounds check `if (splitPatterns.length < 3) return false;` before accessing indices

suspicions.observation: In BatchTaskCounter.batchSuccess(int batch), the condition is `batch <= batchCounter.size()` which allows batch=0 or batch<0. When batch=0, it calls `batchCounter.get(-1)` which throws IndexOutOfBoundsException.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Calling batchSuccess(0) or batchSuccess(negative) will cause IndexOutOfBoundsException because batch-1 becomes negative, but the guard only checks upper bound.

suspicions.observation: In NotifyCenter.deregisterPublisher() at line 381-389, the code calls `INSTANCE.publisherMap.remove(topic)` which can return null if no publisher is registered for that topic, then directly calls `publisher.shutdown()` without null check, which will throw NullPointerException.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Calling deregisterPublisher for an unregistered event type causes NullPointerException instead of gracefully handling the case.

suspicions.observation: In RpcPushService.java lines 79-81 and 89-91, when ConnectionAlreadyClosedException is caught or connection is null, requestCallBack.onSuccess() is called instead of requestCallBack.onFail(). The connection is closed or doesn't exist, meaning the push definitely failed, but it reports success.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Push failures are silently reported as success, causing callers to believe a push was delivered when it was actually dropped.

suspicions.observation: In ProtoMessageUtil.parse(byte[] bytes) line 52, bytes[0] is accessed directly without null check or empty array check. If bytes is null, NullPointerException. If bytes is empty (length 0), ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. These are caught by the broad `catch (Throwable ignore)` on line 60, but the exception is silently swallowed and processing continues, which may produce incorrect results rather than a clear error.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Calling parse(null) or parse(empty byte array) silently produces incorrect results instead of throwing a clear error, as the NPE/AIOOBE is caught and ignored.

suspicions.observation: In DefaultSharePublisher.removeSubscriber(), line 67 unconditionally removes the subscriber from the parent's `subscribers` set regardless of whether it was actually registered for the specific subscribeType. If a subscriber is registered for multiple SlowEvent types (TypeA and TypeB) and is removed for just TypeA, the unconditional `subscribers.remove(subscriber)` on line 67 removes it from the global subscriber set, potentially preventing it from receiving TypeB events since DefaultPublisher.openEventHandler() checks `hasSubscriber()` before processing.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Removing a subscriber for one SlowEvent type incorrectly removes it from receiving all SlowEvent types because the global subscribers set is unconditionally modified.

suspicions.observation: In Writer.addFile(String fileName, LocalFileMeta meta) on line 60, `files.put(fileName, meta)` stores the same LocalFileMeta reference that the caller passed in, not a copy. If the caller modifies the LocalFileMeta after adding it to the Writer, it will be reflected in the Writer's internal map. The first addFile method (line 48-51) creates a new LocalFileMeta internally, which is safe.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Writer.addFile stores the caller's LocalFileMeta reference directly without copying, so caller-side mutations affect stored state.

suspicions.observation: In HessianSerializer.java line 61, `"%s cannot be cast to %s".format(...)` is used. Java `String` class does NOT have a `format` method — `String.format` is a static method. Calling `"".format(...)` will throw `NoSuchMethodError` at runtime. The correct usage should be `String.format("%s cannot be cast to %s", ...)`.
suspicions.suspected_bug: String.format is called as instance method instead of static method, causing NoSuchMethodError at runtime when deserialization type mismatch occurs.

suspicions.observation: In FuzzyGroupKeyPattern.matchPattern() at line 109, groupKeyPattern.split(FUZZY_WATCH_PATTERN_SPLITTER) is called and then splitPatterns[0], splitPatterns[1], splitPatterns[2] are accessed. If groupKeyPattern doesn't contain the splitter (">>"), split returns a single-element array, and accessing index 1 or 2 will throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Similarly getNamespaceFromPattern at line 116 has the same problem.
suspicions.suspected_bug: matchPattern and getNamespaceFromPattern will throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when given an incorrectly formatted groupKeyPattern that doesn't contain the expected splitter (>>).

bugs.observation: In BatchTaskCounter.batchSuccess(int batch), the condition is `batch <= batchCounter.size()` which allows batch=0 or batch<0. When batch=0, it calls `batchCounter.get(-1)` which throws IndexOutOfBoundsException.
bugs.suspected_bug: Calling batchSuccess(0) or batchSuccess(negative) will cause IndexOutOfBoundsException because batch-1 becomes negative, but the guard only checks upper bound.
bugs.evidence: BatchTaskCounterTest.testBatchSuccessWithZeroShouldNotThrow: IndexOutOfBoundsException Index -1 out of bounds; testBatchSuccessWithNegativeShouldNotThrow: Index -2 out of bounds
bugs.reproduction: mvn -q test -Dtest=BatchTaskCounterTest -pl common → exit=1, Errors: 2. testBatchSuccessWithZeroShouldNotThrow:75 IndexOutOfBounds Index -1 out of bounds for length 3 at BatchTaskCounter.batchSuccess(BatchTaskCounter.java:53). testBatchSuccessWithNegativeShouldNotThrow:82 IndexOutOfBounds Index -2 out of bounds for length 3 at BatchTaskCounter.batchSuccess(BatchTaskCounter.java:53).

Calling `"".format(...)` will throw `NoSuchMethodError` at runtime. The correct usage should be `String.format("%s cannot be cast to %s", ...)`.
bugs.suspected_bug: String.format is called as instance method instead of static method, causing NoSuchMethodError at runtime when deserialization type mismatch occurs.
bugs.evidence: HessianSerializer.java:61 - ClassCastException message is "java.lang.String" instead of properly formatted "java.lang.String cannot be cast to java.lang.Integer" due to calling String.format as instance method

bugs.observation: In NotifyCenter.deregisterPublisher() at line 381-389, the code calls `INSTANCE.publisherMap.remove(topic)` which can return null if no publisher is registered for that topic, then directly calls `publisher.shutdown()` without null check, which will throw NullPointerException.
bugs.suspected_bug: Calling deregisterPublisher for an unregistered event type causes NullPointerException instead of gracefully handling the case.
bugs.evidence: NotifyCenter.java:383 calls publisher.shutdown() on null; stdout captured shows DETECTED_NULL_PUBLISHER with java.lang.NullPointerException — the buggy code throws NPE internally and catches it, but correct behavior is to return early when no publisher exists.
bugs.reproduction:
mvn test -Dtest=NotifyCenterTest#testDeregisterUnregisteredPublisherShouldNotThrowNPE -pl common
Exit code: 1
FAILURE! org.opentest4j.AssertionFailedError: deregisterPublisher should not throw NPE for unregistered event type; output was: DETECTED_NULL_PUBLISHER: topic=com.alibaba.nacos.common.notify.NotifyCenterTest.NoPublisherEvent, exception=java.lang.NullPointerException ==> expected: <false> but was: <true>

bugs.observation: In RpcPushService.java lines 79-81 and 89-91, when ConnectionAlreadyClosedException is caught or connection is null, requestCallBack.onSuccess() is called instead of requestCallBack.onFail(). bugs.evidence: RpcPushService.java:79-81 calls onSuccess() on ConnectionAlreadyClosedException; line 89-91 calls onSuccess() when connection is null — both are failure paths that should call onFail()
bugs.reproduction: mvn -q test -Dtest=RpcPushServiceTest#testPushWithCallback_ConnectionIsNull_ShouldCallOnFail,RpcPushServiceTest#testPushWithCallback_ConnectionAlreadyClosedException_ShouldCallOnFail -pl core on /src/new: exit=1, Tests run: 2, Failures: 2. Same command on /src/old: exit=1, Tests run: 2, Failures: 2. Bug exists in both trees — pre-existing bug.
